evidence.field: Early graph analysis and competing identifications
evidence.text: The paper reports that the oracle graph read as 先 is analyzed as 止 plus 人 and used for precedence. It distinguishes this from a similar graph read by different scholars as 先, 侁/姺, or 失/a name; the competing identifications remain unsettled. This does not establish corruption in 先.
evidence.title: 殷墟卜辞中的“先”与“失”

evidence.source: Luo Kun, 殷墟卜辞中的“先”与“失”
evidence.text: The article cites Shang oracle-bone examples including 先祖 (合集 38731), 先酒 (合集 28272), and 先岁 (合集 25615), interpreting them as uses for temporal or ritual-order precedence. The paper assigns no individual artifact dates.
evidence.kind: scholarly article reporting primary inscription examples
evidence.title: 殷墟卜辞中的“先”与“失”

evidence.source: Luo Kun, 殷墟卜辞中的“先”与“失”
evidence.text: The article cites oracle-bone examples in hunting and military contexts, including 合集 28333 and 7283, for going ahead, going forward, or leading. It treats these uses as broadly contemporary with precedence examples and does not establish which sense came first.
evidence.kind: scholarly article reporting primary inscription examples
evidence.title: 殷墟卜辞中的“先”与“失”

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, International Computer Chinese Character and Variant Database
evidence.text: The character-specific record groups oracle-bone, bronze, Chu-slip, and small-seal forms and gives a broad interpretation of a person below a foot, conveying going ahead of others. The text does not establish a complete graphic sequence into modern 先 or identify artifact-level dates for individual forms.
evidence.title: 漢字「先」：字形演變

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, 異體字字典
evidence.field: Received 說文 analysis and modern meanings
evidence.text: The entry records the received 說文 gloss 前進也 and variant transmitted analyses: 大徐本 从几从之 and 段注本 从儿、之. It also lists senses including leading, earlier in time or order, deceased elders, ancient/former, and introductory uses. This later dictionary account is not direct evidence of Shang graphic construction or a full semantic chronology.

gaps: The cited oracle-bone examples are dated only broadly to the Shang corpus; no exact artifact dates were found.
The evidence attests Shang precedence and advancing/leading uses but does not establish their relative chronology or a complete semantic path to later senses such as former/previous.
The Academia Sinica text account does not show a complete graphic sequence into modern 先, nor individual artifact identifiers for the forms.
The similar-looking graph disputed as 失, 侁/姺, or a name remains unresolved; available evidence does not show that 先 itself is a corruption.
The original pixels of the candidate seal-style Commons file could not be opened, and no ancient artifact glyph was visually inspected.
The official Unihan record for U+5148 was inaccessible. The supplied local row gives xiān, but does not establish any historical phonetic relationship; 先 has no proposed sound component here.
No repeatable bulk extract is recommended: character-specific references were sufficient, and permission plus editorial need for a broader extract were not both established.
